subject: Unexpected July usage — request provisional collection freeze
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@brightarc.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightArc Billing <billing@brightarc.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected July usage — request provisional collection freeze

Hi Ben,

We just received the July invoice and noticed a ~4.9x increase in token consumption compared to June (invoice #INV-2026-07-998). This looks wrong — we didn't change any client-side behavior or push any bulk backfills. BrightArc is being flagged for collection this week; can Redwood pause collection while we investigate?

I'm attaching the report we pulled from our side (summary attached). Can you run a backend usage trace and confirm whether these tokens were actually routed to our account or if there was an attribution shift?

Requested next steps:
- Provisional pause on collection and any automatic escalation to collections teams until investigation completes.
- A per-day token breakdown for July and a sample of request IDs around July 14–17.
- If there's an ingestion/backfill event on Redwood's side, we need a proposed remediation and timeline.

Thanks — this is urgent for our finance team.

Samir Patel
Head of Engineering, BrightArc
samir@brightarc.com
+1 415 555 0198

Attachments: usage_export_2026-07_summary.csv (CSV, 45KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@brightarc.com>, BrightArc Billing <billing@brightarc.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected July usage — request provisional collection freeze

Samir — thanks for the flag. Looping in Karthik (billing ops) and Evelyn (CS) to get an urgent trace.

Karthik / Evelyn — can you do the following as priority:
1) Run a token attribution trace for BrightArc account (acct_id: bright-00421) for Jul 1–31, with per-hour granularity.
2) Provide a sample of request IDs and the route (hosted/dedicated/private) for large-days (Jul 14–17).
3) If there was a model re-route or an auxiliary model (e.g., an embed-backfill runner) that consumed tokens, identify root cause and whether we can retroactively adjust attribution.

Samir — I will request a provisional collection freeze from Finance once Karthik confirms whether this is an internal routing/attribution issue. Expect an update within 48 hours.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0123

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@brightarc.com>, BrightArc Billing <billing@brightarc.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected July usage — request provisional collection freeze

Ben / Evelyn / Samir — investigative summary (quick cadence):

Findings (preliminary):
- Token delta: The system shows an additional 9.6M embed tokens attributed to bright-00421 between 2026-07-14T00:00 and 2026-07-17T23:59. Normal monthly baseline for BrightArc is ~2.0M tokens.
- Route: The majority (~88%) of the extra tokens were processed on Hosted API (us-west-2) under the auxiliary embed worker (internal job id: aux-embed-run-924).
- Cause: We have evidence of a backfill job triggered by a misconfigured customer migration pipeline that re-submitted historical documents. The job used a service account that had been mistakenly tagged to BrightArc's account namespace due to a tenant-tagging edge case.

Evidence attached: usage_export_2026-07_detailed.csv (per-request lines), forensic_query.sql (the aggregation query run to isolate requestids), and a short drive folder with logs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-brightarc-audit

Recommended remediation path:
1) Provisional credit: Recommend issuing a provisional credit equal to 30% of the disputed amount while we run a full audit (this covers the bulk of inadvertent backfill while retaining incentive for final reconciliation).
2) Collection: Request Finance to pause collection for invoice INV-2026-07-998 and flag for manual review.
3) Technical mitigation: We will patch the tenant-labeling logic and add a stop-gap filter on auxiliary workers to ignore requests without explicit BrightArc auth headers. Patch ETA: 5 business days.
4) Final reconciliation: After audit, either confirm full credit or net a smaller adjustment.

Notes on confidence: high for the root cause (tenant-tagging). We can produce a per-request id list for re-ingestion if BrightArc wants to independently verify.

Karthik Iyer
Billing & Metering Ops, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: usage_export_2026-07_detailed.csv (CSV, 2.2MB); forensic_query.sql (TEXT, 3KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@brightarc.com>, BrightArc Billing <billing@brightarc.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected July usage — request provisional collection freeze

Samir — thanks for your patience while we investigated. Per Karthik's forensic trace we're confident this was an internal attribution issue caused by an auxiliary backfill job.

Actions we've taken (today):
- Finance has applied a provisional credit memo for 30% of invoice INV-2026-07-998 (credit memo attached: credit_memo_draft.pdf). This will appear on your account as a provisional adjustment pending the full audit.
- Collections have been paused for this invoice until 2026-08-25 (manual hold).
- Engineering has scheduled a backfill filter patch; expected deploy in 5 business days.

Next steps for BrightArc:
- If you would like a complete list of request IDs for independent verification, reply and we'll share a scoped export (Karthik attached the query he used).
- We'll follow up with a final reconciliation email when the audit completes; if further credit is warranted we'll escalate for approvals.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0123
